# Design plan:
# - 4 observations per participant (m = 4)
# - Marginal SD = 1
# - Intraclass correlation = 0.4
# - Mean group difference = 0.45
# - Equal allocation to two groups (1:1)
# - Two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# - Target power = 0.90

# Step 1: Calculate the variance of participant-level averages
m <- 4  # observations per participant
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
sigma <- 1  # marginal SD

# Within-participant variance component: sigma_u^2 = rho * sigma^2
# Between-participant variance component: sigma_e^2 = (1 - rho) * sigma^2
# Variance of participant average = sigma^2 * [(1 - rho) / m + rho]
var_avg <- sigma^2 * ((1 - rho) / m + rho)
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat("Variance structure:\n")
cat("Marginal variance:", sigma^2, "\n")
cat("Intraclass correlation:", rho, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant:", m, "\n")
cat("Variance of participant average:", var_avg, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Set up parameters for sample size calculation
delta <- 0.45  # mean group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# For two-sample t-test with equal variances and equal group sizes:
# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = delta / (sd_avg * sqrt(2/n))
# where n is the sample size per group
# Critical value for two-sided test: t_alpha/2,2n-2
# Power = P(|T| > t_alpha/2,2n-2 | lambda)

# We need to invert the power function to find n such that power(n) = target_power

# The standardized effect size (Cohen's d) using the pooled SD
cohens_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effect size analysis:\n")
cat("Mean group difference:", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Cohen's d (standardized effect size):", cohens_d, "\n\n")

# Use the t-test power formula
# For a two-sample t-test with equal variances and n per group:
# noncentrality parameter λ = δ / SE = δ / (sd_avg * sqrt(2/n))
# df = 2n - 2

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size per group
power_t_test <- function(n, delta, sd_avg, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "two.sided") {
  # Critical value (two-sided test)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = 2*n - 2)
  
  # Standard error of difference in means
  se_diff <- sd_avg * sqrt(2/n)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- delta / se_diff
  
  # Power: P(|T| > t_crit | lambda) under non-central t distribution
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df = 2*n - 2, ncp = lambda) + 
           (1 - pt(t_crit, df = 2*n - 2, ncp = lambda))
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n (integer) such that power >= target_power
# Start with a reasonable upper bound
n_candidates <- seq(1, 200, by = 1)
power_values <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) power_t_test(n, delta, sd_avg, alpha))

# Find the minimum n where power >= target_power
min_n <- min(n_candidates[power_values >= target_power])
power_at_min <- power_t_test(min_n, delta, sd_avg, alpha)
power_at_prev <- ifelse(min_n > 1, power_t_test(min_n - 1, delta, sd_avg, alpha), NA)

cat("Sample size search results:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", power_at_min, "\n")
if (!is.na(power_at_prev)) {
  cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", power_at_prev, "\n")
}
cat("\n")

# This requires specifying the effect size in terms of the SD of the participant average

  n = min_n,
  delta = delta,
  sd = sd_avg,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)

cat("Verification using power.t.test():\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", power_check$power, "\n\n")

  n_per_group = n_candidates[1:min(50, length(n_candidates))],
  power = power_values[1:min(50, length(n_candidates))]
)

cat("Sample size and power table (first 50 values):\n")
print(head(summary_table[summary_table$n_per_group >= max(1, min_n - 5) & 
                        summary_table$n_per_group <= min_n + 5, ], 15))

cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group for 90% power:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_at_min, "\n")

# Two-group random-intercept Gaussian study with repeated measures
# Design plan:
# - 4 observations per participant (m = 4)
# - Marginal SD = 1
# - Intraclass correlation = 0.4
# - Mean group difference = 0.45
# - Equal allocation to two groups (1:1)
# - Two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# - Target power = 0.90

# Step 1: Calculate the variance of participant-level averages
m <- 4  # observations per participant
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
sigma <- 1  # marginal SD

# Within-participant variance component: sigma_u^2 = rho * sigma^2
# Between-participant variance component: sigma_e^2 = (1 - rho) * sigma^2
# Variance of participant average = sigma^2 * [(1 - rho) / m + rho]
var_avg <- sigma^2 * ((1 - rho) / m + rho)
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat("Variance structure:\n")
cat("Marginal variance:", sigma^2, "\n")
cat("Intraclass correlation:", rho, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant:", m, "\n")
cat("Variance of participant average:", var_avg, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Set up parameters for sample size calculation
delta <- 0.45  # mean group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# For two-sample t-test with equal variances and equal group sizes:
# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = delta / (sd_avg * sqrt(2/n))
# where n is the sample size per group
# Critical value for two-sided test: t_alpha/2,2n-2
# Power = P(|T| > t_alpha/2,2n-2 | lambda)

# We need to invert the power function to find n such that power(n) = target_power

# The standardized effect size (Cohen's d) using the pooled SD
cohens_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effect size analysis:\n")
cat("Mean group difference:", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Cohen's d (standardized effect size):", cohens_d, "\n\n")

# Use the t-test power formula
# For a two-sample t-test with equal variances and n per group:
# noncentrality parameter λ = δ / SE = δ / (sd_avg * sqrt(2/n))
# df = 2n - 2

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size per group
power_t_test <- function(n, delta, sd_avg, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "two.sided") {
  # Critical value (two-sided test)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = 2*n - 2)
  
  # Standard error of difference in means
  se_diff <- sd_avg * sqrt(2/n)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- delta / se_diff
  
  # Power: P(|T| > t_crit | lambda) under non-central t distribution
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df = 2*n - 2, ncp = lambda) + 
           (1 - pt(t_crit, df = 2*n - 2, ncp = lambda))
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n (integer) such that power >= target_power
# Start with a reasonable upper bound
n_candidates <- seq(1, 200, by = 1)
power_values <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) power_t_test(n, delta, sd_avg, alpha))

# Find the minimum n where power >= target_power
min_n <- min(n_candidates[power_values >= target_power])
power_at_min <- power_t_test(min_n, delta, sd_avg, alpha)
power_at_prev <- ifelse(min_n > 1, power_t_test(min_n - 1, delta, sd_avg, alpha), NA)

cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", power_at_min, "\n")

}

# This requires specifying the effect size in terms of the SD of the participant average

)

  n_per_group = n_candidates[1:min(50, length(n_candidates))],
  power = power_values[1:min(50, length(n_candidates))]
)

print(head(summary_table[summary_table$n_per_group >= max(1, min_n - 5) & 
                        summary_table$n_per_group <= min_n + 5, ], 15))

cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group for 90% power:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_at_min, "\n")

# Two-group random-intercept Gaussian study with repeated measures
# Design plan:
# - 4 observations per participant (m = 4)
# - Marginal SD = 1
# - Intraclass correlation = 0.4
# - Mean group difference = 0.45
# - Equal allocation to two groups (1:1)
# - Two-sided pooled t-test at alpha = 0.05
# - Target power = 0.90

# Step 1: Calculate the variance of participant-level averages
m <- 4  # observations per participant
rho <- 0.4  # intraclass correlation
sigma <- 1  # marginal SD

# Within-participant variance component: sigma_u^2 = rho * sigma^2
# Between-participant variance component: sigma_e^2 = (1 - rho) * sigma^2
# Variance of participant average = sigma^2 * [(1 - rho) / m + rho]
var_avg <- sigma^2 * ((1 - rho) / m + rho)
sd_avg <- sqrt(var_avg)

cat("Variance structure:\n")
cat("Marginal variance:", sigma^2, "\n")
cat("Intraclass correlation:", rho, "\n")
cat("Observations per participant:", m, "\n")
cat("Variance of participant average:", var_avg, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", sd_avg, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Set up parameters for sample size calculation
delta <- 0.45  # mean group difference
alpha <- 0.05  # significance level (two-sided)
target_power <- 0.90

# For two-sample t-test with equal variances and equal group sizes:
# Noncentrality parameter: lambda = delta / (sd_avg * sqrt(2/n))
# where n is the sample size per group
# Critical value for two-sided test: t_alpha/2,2n-2
# Power = P(|T| > t_alpha/2,2n-2 | lambda)

# We need to invert the power function to find n such that power(n) = target_power

# The standardized effect size (Cohen's d) using the pooled SD
cohens_d <- delta / sd_avg

cat("Effect size analysis:\n")
cat("Mean group difference:", delta, "\n")
cat("SD of participant average:", sd_avg, "\n")
cat("Cohen's d (standardized effect size):", cohens_d, "\n\n")

# Use the t-test power formula
# For a two-sample t-test with equal variances and n per group:
# noncentrality parameter λ = δ / SE = δ / (sd_avg * sqrt(2/n))
# df = 2n - 2

library(stats)

# Function to calculate power for a given sample size per group
power_t_test <- function(n, delta, sd_avg, alpha = 0.05, alternative = "two.sided") {
  # Critical value (two-sided test)
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = 2*n - 2)
  
  # Standard error of difference in means
  se_diff <- sd_avg * sqrt(2/n)
  
  # Noncentrality parameter
  lambda <- delta / se_diff
  
  # Power: P(|T| > t_crit | lambda) under non-central t distribution
  power <- pt(-t_crit, df = 2*n - 2, ncp = lambda) + 
           (1 - pt(t_crit, df = 2*n - 2, ncp = lambda))
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n (integer) such that power >= target_power
# Start with a reasonable upper bound
n_candidates <- seq(1, 200, by = 1)
power_values <- sapply(n_candidates, function(n) power_t_test(n, delta, sd_avg, alpha))

# Find the minimum n where power >= target_power
min_n <- min(n_candidates[power_values >= target_power])
power_at_min <- power_t_test(min_n, delta, sd_avg, alpha)
power_at_prev <- ifelse(min_n > 1, power_t_test(min_n - 1, delta, sd_avg, alpha), NA)

cat("Sample size search results:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size per group:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", power_at_min, "\n")
if (!is.na(power_at_prev)) {
  cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", power_at_prev, "\n")
}
cat("\n")

# Step 3: Verify the calculation using alternative method
# Double-check with power.t.test (standard two-sample t-test)
# This requires specifying the effect size in terms of the SD of the participant average

power_check <- power.t.test(
  n = min_n,
  delta = delta,
  sd = sd_avg,
  sig.level = alpha,
  type = "two.sample",
  alternative = "two.sided"
)

cat("Verification using power.t.test():\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", power_check$power, "\n\n")

# Step 4: Create a summary table of power values around the minimum
summary_table <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = n_candidates[1:min(50, length(n_candidates))],
  power = power_values[1:min(50, length(n_candidates))]
)

cat("Sample size and power table (first 50 values):\n")
print(head(summary_table[summary_table$n_per_group >= max(1, min_n - 5) & 
                        summary_table$n_per_group <= min_n + 5, ], 15))

cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Minimum participants per group for 90% power:", min_n, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_at_min, "\n")
